examples.trans: We need to do even more.

Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: in questions: а вдруг...? = and what if...?
А вдруг... = what if. Core Russian adv meaning 'suddenly; all of a sudden' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'годный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('profitable / advantageous').

examples.text: По-моему, это просто отличный и выгодный бизнес.
examples.trans: In my opinion, it is simply great and profitable business.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень выгодный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very profitable choice.

meanings.note: after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: An idiom for a big telling-off. Common feminine noun meaning 'head' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: 'голову оторвать' = to tear someone's head off
meanings.note: An idiom for a big telling-off. Common feminine noun meaning 'head' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Mum will tear my head off.

examples.text: Какая тебе опергруппа? Мне твоя мать голову оторвёт.
examples.trans: What field team? Your mother will tear my head off.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
Дай! = give (me)!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.

meanings.note: Colloquial. Common neuter noun meaning 'good, kindness' in everyday Russian.
Colloquial. Common neuter noun meaning 'good, kindness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Good deeds come back to the sender.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'виснуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'froze up / spaced out'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и зависнуть вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and froze up on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют зависнуть.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to froze up.

meanings.note: + dative of person. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'платить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pay', paired with 'платить'.

examples.trans: I have already paid for dinner.

examples.text: И денег я тебе заплачу. В десять раз больше!
examples.trans: And I'll pay you money. Ten times more!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hello'.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Comparative of хорошо. Core Russian adv meaning 'better' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Два года назад = two years ago. Core Russian adv meaning 'ago; back, backwards' in everyday speech.
Шаг назад = a step back. Core Russian adv meaning 'ago; back, backwards' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

оформить.gloss: to register officially, file properly, draw up

meanings.en: to draw up, file, register officially
meanings.note: оформлены верно = properly filed/registered

examples.trans: All the signatures are properly filed.
We drew up the documents quickly.

examples.text: Ведь нет. Подписи собраны и все оформлены верно.
examples.trans: Actually, no. The signatures are collected and all properly filed.

meanings.note: Палец на ноге. Common masculine noun meaning 'finger; toe' in everyday Russian.
Палец на ноге. Common masculine noun meaning 'finger; toe' in everyday Russian.
Parenthetical. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-моему').

examples.text: Да, по-моему, здорово! Сколько сил в этой машине?
examples.trans: Yes, I think it's great! How much power does this car have?

meanings.note: in greeting formula добро пожаловать

examples.text: Очень приятно познакомиться. Добро пожаловать к нам!
examples.trans: Very nice to meet you. Welcome to our team!

examples.text: Добро пожаловать в наш новый дом!

examples.trans: The guests arrived right at lunchtime.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'резать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to cut', forming an aspectual pair with 'резать'.

examples.trans: The cook sliced the bread into pieces.

examples.text: Он же тебя просто на куски порежет!
examples.trans: After all, he will simply slice you into pieces!

meanings.note: Последний раз = for the last time. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'следний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last, final').

examples.trans: I'm asking for the last time.
I'm asking for the last time. Where is the money?

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Colloquial. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('empty').
Colloquial. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('empty').

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: в следующий раз = next time; следующий! = next, please!

examples.text: А ты в следующий раз на мои деньги не рассчитывай. И всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Well, next time don't count on my money. And everything will be fine.

meanings.note: Сломать руку = to break one's arm. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break', paired with 'ломать'.

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.

meanings.note: Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').
Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: За спиной = behind one's back. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пина'). Common feminine noun meaning 'back (body part)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: для страховки = just to be safe, as insurance

examples.trans: And for insurance, a Buddhist temple too!

examples.text: Перед поездкой он оформил медицинскую страховку.
examples.trans: Before the trip he took out medical insurance.
